nodes.statement: The set of extended non-negative real numbers is $\mathbb{R}_{+,\infty} = \mathbb{R}_{+} \cup \{+\infty\}$.
nodes.section: 1 Extended real numbers and their integral
nodes.label: def:ENNReal

nodes.statement: The set of extended real numbers is $\overline{\mathbb{R}} = \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty, -\infty\}$.
nodes.section: 1 Extended real numbers and their integral
nodes.label: def:EReal

nodes.statement: The logarithm as a function from $\mathbb{R}_{+, \infty}$ to $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is defined as \begin{align*} \log(x) &= \begin{cases} -\infty & \text{if } x = 0 \\ \text{the usual logarithm} & \text{if } x \in (0, +\infty) \\ +\infty & \text{if } x = +\infty \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.section: 1 Extended real numbers and their integral
nodes.label: def:ENNReal.log

nodes.statement: For $f : \Omega \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ and $\mu$ a measure on $\Omega$, we define the extended integral of $f$ with respect to $\mu$ as \begin{align*} \int_{\omega} f (\omega) \, d\mu &:= \int_{\omega} f^{+} (\omega) \, d\mu - \int_{\omega} f^{-} (\omega) \, d\mu \: , \end{align*} where $f^{+} = \max(f, 0)$ and $f^{-} = -\min(f, 0)$, and their integrals are Lebesgue integrals, possibly taking the value $+\infty$.
nodes.section: 1 Extended real numbers and their integral
nodes.label: def:eintegral

nodes.statement: An E-variable for a set of probability measures $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ is a measurable function $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ such that for all $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, $Q[f] \le 1$.
nodes.label: def:eVar

nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{P} \subseteq \mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ then $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}} \subseteq \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{P}}$.
nodes.label: lem:eVarSet_anti

nodes.statement: A randomized E-variable for a set of distributions $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ is a Markov kernel $\eta : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ such that for all $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, $(\eta \circ Q)[\mathrm{id}] \le 1$.
nodes.label: def:randEVar

nodes.statement: A Markov kernel $\eta : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ is a randomized E-variable for a set of probability measures $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ if and only if the measurable function $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ defined by $f(x) = \eta(x)[\mathrm{id}]$ is an E-variable for $\mathcal{Q}$.
nodes.label: lem:randEVar_iff_eVar

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of measures. A set $S \subseteq \mathcal{X}$ is said to be $\mathcal{Q}$-null if $Q[S] = 0$ for all $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$. A property $p : \mathcal{X} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is said to hold $\mathcal{Q}$-almost everywhere (denoted by $\mathcal{Q}$-a.e.) if the set $\{x \mid \neg p(x)\}$ is $\mathcal{Q}$-null.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.label: def:aeSet

nodes.statement: A set $S \subseteq \mathcal{X}$ has a $\mathcal{Q}$-null complement iff $S \in \bigsqcup_{Q \in \mathcal{Q}} \mathrm{ae}_Q$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.label: lem:aeSet_filter

nodes.statement: By definition of the $\mathrm{ae}$ filter and of a supremum of filters.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures

nodes.statement: Let $P \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X})$ and let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of measures. We say that $P$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathcal{Q}$ (denoted by $P \ll \mathcal{Q}$) if all $\mathcal{Q}$-null sets are $P$-null sets.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.label: def:acSet

nodes.statement: Let $P \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X})$ and let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X})$. Then $P \ll \mathcal{Q}$ iff $\mathrm{ae}_P \le \bigsqcup_{Q \in \mathcal{Q}} \mathrm{ae}_Q$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.label: lem:acSet_iff

nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures

nodes.statement: For $P \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X})$, there is a unique decomposition $P = P_{\mathrm{ac}} + P_{\perp}$ with $P_{\mathrm{ac}} \ll \mathcal{Q}$ and $P_{\perp} \perp \mathcal{Q}$ (meaning that there exists a $\mathcal{Q}$-null set $A$ with $P_{\perp}(A^c) = 0$).
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.label: lem:RN_acSet

nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures

nodes.statement: The singular set of $P$ with respect to $\mathcal{Q}$ is a $\mathcal{Q}$-null set $A$ such that the singular part $P_{\perp}$ satisfies $P_{\perp}(A^c) = 0$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.label: def:singularSet

nodes.statement: The singular set of $P$ with respect to $\mathcal{Q}$ is unique up to $P$ and $\mathcal{Q}$-null sets.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.label: lem:singularSet_unique

nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of probability measures and let $f$ be an E-variable for $\mathcal{Q}$. Then the set $\{f = \infty\}$ is $\mathcal{Q}$-null.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.label: lem:nullSet_eq_top

nodes.statement: Let $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$. Since $f$ is an E-variable for $\mathcal{Q}$, we have $Q[f] \le 1$. Hence $Q[\{f = \infty\}] = 0$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures

nodes.statement: We call utility a function $U : \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ which is non-decreasing, concave, finite except perhaps at 0 and $\infty$, continuous, and continuously differentiable on $(0, \infty)$.
nodes.label: def:Utility

nodes.statement: The logarithm satisfies the properties of a utility function and we call it logarithmic utility.
nodes.label: def:logUtility

nodes.statement: For a utility function $U$, the maximal utility for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$ is defined as \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) &= \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)] \: , \end{align*} in which the expectation is the extended integral defined in Definition~\ref{def:eintegral}.
nodes.label: def:maxUtility

nodes.statement: For a utility function $U$, the maximal randomized utility for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$ is defined as \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}^R(P, \mathcal{Q}) &= \sup_{\eta \in \mathcal{E}^R_{\mathcal{Q}}} (\eta \circ P)[U] \: , \end{align*} in which the expectation is the extended integral defined in Definition~\ref{def:eintegral}.
nodes.label: def:maxRandUtility

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{Q}' \subseteq \mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}') &\ge \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_anti

nodes.statement: Let $U : \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ be a utility function and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ a set of probability measures. Let $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}^R(P, \mathcal{Q}) &= \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxRandUtility_eq_maxUtility

nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}} \subseteq \mathcal{E}^R_{\mathcal{Q}}$, the left hand side is greater than or equal to the right hand side. For the other direction, let $\eta \in \mathcal{E}^R_{\mathcal{Q}}$ be a randomized E-variable. By concavity of $U$, \begin{align*} (\eta \circ P)[U] &= P[x \mapsto \eta(x)[U]] \le P[x \mapsto U(\eta(x)[\mathrm{id}])] \end{align*} The function $x \mapsto \eta(x)[\mathrm{id}]$ is a measurable function and belongs to $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.

Suppose that there exists an event $A$ such that $P(A) > 0$ and $Q(A) = 0$ for all $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$. That is, we don't have $P \ll \mathcal{Q}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) &= +\infty \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_eq_top_of_not_acSet

nodes.statement: The function $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ defined by $f(x) = +\infty$ if $x \in A$ and $f(x) = 0$ otherwise is an E-variable for $\mathcal{Q}$ since $Q[f] = 0$ for all $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$. \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge P[\log f] = P(A) \cdot (+\infty) = +\infty \: . \end{align*}
The function $R \mapsto \mathcal{U}(R, \mathcal{P})$ is convex.
nodes.label: lem:convex_maxUtility

nodes.statement: Let $R_1, R_2 \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and let $\theta \in [0,1]$. \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(\theta R_1 + (1 - \theta) R_2, \mathcal{P}) &= \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{P}}} (\theta R_1 + (1 - \theta) R_2)\left[\log f\right] \\ &= \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{P}}} \left\{\theta R_1[\log f] + (1 - \theta) R_2[\log f]\right\} \\ &\le \theta \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{P}}} R_1[\log f] + (1 - \theta) \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{P}}} R_2[\log f] \\ &= \theta \mathcal{U}(R_1, \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \theta) \mathcal{U}(R_2, \mathcal{P}) \: . \end{align*}

Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of probability measures and let $\phi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a measurable function. Then for all $g \in \mathcal{E}_{\phi_* \mathcal{Q}}$, $g \circ \phi \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
nodes.label: lem:eVar_comp

nodes.statement: For $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, \begin{align*} Q[g \circ \phi] &= (\phi_* Q)[g] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}

Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of probability measures and let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be a Markov kernel. Then for all $\xi \in \mathcal{E}_{\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}}^R$, $\xi \circ \kappa \in \mathcal{E}^R_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
nodes.label: lem:randEVar_comp

nodes.statement: For $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, \begin{align*} ((\xi \circ \kappa) \circ Q)[\mathrm{id}] &= (\xi \circ (\kappa \circ Q))[\mathrm{id}] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}

nodes.name: Data processing inequality with randomized e-variables
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of probability measures and $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Let $U : \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ be a utility function. Then for all Markov kernels $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$, \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}^R(P, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \mathcal{U}^R(\kappa \circ P, \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: thm:maxRandUtility_comp_le

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:randEVar_comp}, $\{\xi \circ \kappa \mid \xi \in \mathcal{E}^R_{\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}}\} \subseteq \mathcal{E}^R_{\mathcal{Q}}$, hence \begin{align*} \sup_{\eta \in \mathcal{E}^R_{\mathcal{Q}}} (\eta \circ P)[U] &\ge \sup_{\eta \in \{\xi \circ \kappa \mid \xi \in \mathcal{E}^R_{\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}}\}} (\eta \circ P)[U] = \sup_{\xi \in \mathcal{E}^R_{\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}}} (\xi \circ \kappa \circ P)[U] \: . \end{align*}

nodes.name: Data processing inequality with e-variables
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be a Markov kernel, $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(\kappa \circ P, \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}) &\le \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_comp_le

nodes.statement: We can use Lemma~\ref{lem:maxRandUtility_eq_maxUtility} to obtain the data-processing with a Markov kernel for e-variables from the result for randomized e-variables (Theorem~\ref{thm:maxRandUtility_comp_le}).

nodes.name: Data processing inequality with e-variables
nodes.statement: Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a measurable function, $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(f_*P, f_* \mathcal{Q}) &\le \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_map_le

nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_comp_le} with the deterministic Markov kernel given by $f$.

Let $\phi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a measurable embedding, $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(\phi_* P, \phi_* \mathcal{Q}) &= \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_map_eq

nodes.statement: Let $R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$, $\mathcal{P} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and let $\phi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$ be a measurable map such that $\phi \circ \phi = \mathrm{id}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(R, \phi_* \mathcal{P}) &= \mathcal{U}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{P}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_map_swap

nodes.statement: To prove the first inequality, we use Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_map_le}: \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(R, \phi_* \mathcal{P}) &= \mathcal{U}(\phi_* (\phi_* R), \phi_* \mathcal{P}) \\ &\le \mathcal{U}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{P}) \: . \end{align*} For the reverse inequality, \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{P}) &= \mathcal{U}(\phi_* R, \phi_* (\phi_* \mathcal{P})) \\ &\le \mathcal{U}(R, \phi_* \mathcal{P}) \: . \end{align*}

Let $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. A numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$ is a $P$-almost surely positive e-variable $f^* \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ such that $P[f / f^*] \le 1$ for all $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$~.
nodes.label: def:IsNumeraire

nodes.statement: Let $f^*$ be a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$ and let $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$. Then $P\left[\log \frac{f}{f^*}\right] \le 0$.
nodes.label: lem:IsNumeraire.eintegral_log_div_nonpos

nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a $P$-almost surely positive E-variable for a set of probability measures $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then $f$ is a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$ if and only if $P[\log \frac{g}{f}] \le 0$ for all $g \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
nodes.label: lem:numeraire_iff_logOptimal

nodes.statement: Let $f^*$ be a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$. Then for all $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$, \begin{align*} P[\log f] &\le P[\log f^*] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:IsNumeraire.eintegral_log_le

nodes.statement: Let $f^*$ be a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$. Then $P[\log f^*] \ge 0$.
nodes.label: lem:IsNumeraire.eintegral_log_nonneg

nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{lem:IsNumeraire.eintegral_log_le} with the e-variable $f = 1$.
Let $\mathcal{Q}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{Q}_2$. If $f^*$ is a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q}_1)$ and $f^* \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_2}$ then $f^*$ is also a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q}_2)$.
nodes.label: lem:numeraire_mono

nodes.statement: For $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_2}$, we have $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1}$ since $\mathcal{Q}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{Q}_2$. Then $P\left[f/f^*\right] \le 1$ by the numeraire property for $(P, \mathcal{Q}_1)$. Thus $f^*$ is a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q}_2)$.

Let $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. If $f^*$ is a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$ then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(P, \mathcal{Q}) &= P[U(f^*)] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_eq_integral

nodes.statement: Let $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of measurable functions from $\mathcal{X}$ to $\mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ and let $Q \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. There exists a sequence of measurable functions $\tilde{X}_n \in \mathrm{conv}(X_n, X_{n+1}, \ldots)$ and $X : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+, \infty}$ such that $\tilde{X}_n \to X$ $Q$-almost surely.
nodes.label: lem:exists_mem_conv_tendsto

nodes.statement: Proved in the Brownian motion project.

Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of probability measures and $U : \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ a concave function which is bounded from above. Then there exists $f^* \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ such that \begin{align*} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)] &= P[U(f^*)] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:exists_integral_utility_eq_sup

nodes.statement: Let $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of e-variables in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ such that $n \mapsto P[U(f_n)]$ is non-decreasing and $P[U(f_n)] \to \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)]$. Let $\tilde{f}_n$ be a sequence of measurable functions and let $\tilde{f} : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+, \infty}$, with $\tilde{f}_n \in \mathrm{conv}(f_n, f_{n+1}, \ldots)$ such that $\tilde{f}_n \to \tilde{f}$ $P$-almost surely. That sequence exists by Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_mem_conv_tendsto}. By convexity of $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$, $\tilde{f}_n \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ for all $n$. Let $f^* = \liminf_{n \to \infty} \tilde{f}_n$. Note that $f^*$ is a measurable function such that $f^* = \tilde{f}$ $P$-almost surely. We have $f^* \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ by an application of Fatou's lemma: for $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, \begin{align*} Q[f^*] = Q[\liminf_{n \to \infty} \tilde{f}_n] \le \liminf_{n \to \infty} Q[\tilde{f}_n] \le 1 \: . \end{align*} By concavity of $U$ and the fact that $P[U(f_n)]$ is non-decreasing, we have \begin{align*} P[U(\tilde{f}_n)] &= P[U(\sum_{i=n}^{m_n} \lambda_{n,i} f_{i})] \ge \sum_{i=n}^{m_n} \lambda_{n,i} P[U(f_{i})] \ge P[U(f_n)] \: . \end{align*} We also have $f^* = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \tilde{f}_n$ $P$-almost surely, hence by Fatou's lemma (using that $U$ is bounded from above), \begin{align*} P[U(f^*)] &= P[U(\limsup_{n \to \infty} \tilde{f}_n)] \ge \limsup_{n \to \infty} P[U(\tilde{f}_n)] \ge \limsup_{n \to \infty} P[U(f_n)] = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)] \: . \end{align*} Since $f^* \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$, we also have $P[U(f^*)] \le \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)]$, which proves the equality.

Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of probability measures and $U : \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ a concave function which is bounded from above. Then there exists $f^* \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ such that \begin{align*} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)] &= P[U(f^*)] \: , \end{align*} and such that all e-variables are $P$-a.s. finite on $\{f^* < \infty\}$.
nodes.label: lem:exists_integral_utility_eq_sup_forall_lt_top

nodes.statement: Let $f_0$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_integral_utility_eq_sup}. The set $\{f_0 = \infty\}$ is $\mathcal{Q}$-null by Lemma~\ref{lem:nullSet_eq_top}. TODO

Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of probability measures and $U : \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}}$ a non-decreasing concave $C^1$ function which is bounded from above. Then the e-variable $f^*$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_integral_utility_eq_sup} is such that for all e-variables $g \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$, \begin{align*} P\left[ U'(f^*) (g - f^*) \right] \le 0 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:bounded_numeraire_first_order

nodes.statement: For $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$, let $f_t = t f + (1-t) f^*$ for $t \in [0,1]$. By concavity of $U$, $U(f_t) \ge t U(f) + (1-t) U(f^*)$, hence \begin{align*} \frac{U(f_t) - U(f^*)}{t} &\ge U(f) - U(f^*) \: . \end{align*} TODO

nodes.name: Existence of the numeraire
nodes.statement: Let $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. A numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q})$ exists and is $P$-a.e. unique.
nodes.label: thm:exists_numeraire

nodes.name: Numeraire of a product
nodes.statement: Let $P_1 \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X}), P_2 \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y})$ and $\mathcal{Q}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X}), \mathcal{Q}_2 \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y})$. Then the numeraire for the product $(P_1 \times P_2, \mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2)$ is given by the product of the numeraires for $(P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1)$ and $(P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2)$: \begin{align*} E^*_{P_1 \times P_2, \mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2} &= E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1} E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2} \: . \end{align*} Its logarithmic utility is given by \begin{align*} (P_1 \times P_2)[\log E^*_{P_1 \times P_2, \mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2}] &= P_1[\log E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1}] + P_2[\log E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: thm:numeraire_prod

nodes.statement: We first need to check that $E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1} E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2}$. For $Q_1 \in \mathcal{Q}_1$ and $Q_2 \in \mathcal{Q}_2$, we have \begin{align*} (Q_1 \times Q_2)\left[E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1} E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}\right] &= Q_1[E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1}] Q_2[E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}] \le 1 \: . \end{align*} Let's now check the numeraire property. Let $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2}$. Let $E^*_1 = E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1}$ and $E^*_2 = E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}$. \begin{align*} (P_1 \times P_2)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_1 E^*_2} \right] &= P_1\left[\frac{1}{E_1^*}P_2\left[\frac{f}{E^*_2}\right] \right] \: . \end{align*} If we can show that $x \mapsto P_2\left[\frac{f(x, \cdot)}{E^*_2}\right]$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1}$, then we can apply the definition of the numeraire for $(P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1)$ to obtain \begin{align*} (P_1 \times P_2)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_1 E^*_2} \right] &= P_1\left[\frac{1}{E_1^*}P_2\left[\frac{f}{E^*_2}\right] \right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*} Let then $Q_1 \in \mathcal{Q}_1$. We want to show that $Q_1 \left[P_2\left[\frac{f(x, \cdot)}{E^*_2}\right]\right] \le 1$. By Fubini's theorem, we have \begin{align*} Q_1 \left[P_2\left[\frac{f(x, \cdot)}{E^*_2}\right]\right] &= P_2\left[\frac{Q_1 \left[f(\cdot, y)\right]}{E^*_2}\right] \: . \end{align*} It now suffices to show that $y \mapsto Q_1 \left[f(\cdot, y)\right]$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_2}$. Let $Q_2 \in \mathcal{Q}_2$. Then \begin{align*} Q_2\left[y \mapsto Q_1 \left[f(\cdot, y)\right]\right] = (Q_1 \times Q_2)\left[f\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*} The last inequality holds since $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2}$.

Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $H \subseteq (\mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y})$ be a set of Markov kernels. If $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}\otimes H}$ then for all $\eta \in H$, the function $x \mapsto \eta(x)[f(x, \cdot)]$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
nodes.label: lem:eVar_integral_kernel

nodes.statement: For $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$ and $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}\otimes H}$, $Q[x \mapsto \eta(x)[f]] = (Q \otimes \eta)[f] \le 1$, hence $(x \mapsto \eta(x)[f(x, \cdot)]) \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
$E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, \mathcal{Q} \otimes \kappa} =_{(P\otimes \kappa) a.e.} (x, y) \mapsto E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}(x)$ for any Markov kernel $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$.
nodes.label: lem:numeraire_compProd_same_kernel

nodes.statement: First we need to show that $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes \kappa}$. It is measurable and for $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, \begin{align*} (Q \otimes \kappa)\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}\right] = Q\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*} We then check the numeraire condition. By Lemma~\ref{lem:eVar_integral_kernel}, $(x \mapsto \kappa(x)[f]) \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$. By the definition of the numeraire, we then have \begin{align*} P\left[\frac{\kappa(x)[f]}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}}\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*} That is, $(P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}}\right] \le 1$ for all $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}\otimes \kappa}$. We have proved that $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}$ is the numeraire for $(P \otimes \kappa, \mathcal{Q} \otimes \kappa)$.

For any $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$, we have \begin{align*} (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, \{P\} \otimes H}}\right] &\le 1 \: . \end{align*} Note that this proves the numeraire property for the candidate $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}$, but we don't know if it is an e-variable, so can't conclude that it's the numeraire. As a consequence, \begin{align*} (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\log E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, \mathcal{Q} \otimes H}\right] \le P\left[\log E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}\right] + (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\log E^*_{P\otimes \kappa, \{P\} \otimes H}\right] \: . \end{align*} If $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, \{P\} \otimes H}$ was an e-variable, then we would have equality.
nodes.label: thm:numeraire_compProd_le

nodes.statement: Let $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$. \begin{align*} (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}}\right] &= (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f/E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}}{E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}}\right] \: . \end{align*} It suffices to show that $f/E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{P \otimes H}$ to obtain that this is less than 1 by the numeraire property. Let $\eta \in H$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:numeraire_compProd_same_kernel}, \begin{align*} (P \otimes \eta) \left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}}\right] &= (P \otimes \eta) \left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P \otimes \eta, \mathcal{Q} \otimes \eta}}\right] \end{align*} and since $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$ it is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes \eta}$ and the numeraire property gives that this ratio is less than or equal to 1. We conclude that $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}$ satisfies the numeraire property. We then have \begin{align*} (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\log \frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}}\right] &\le \log \left( (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}}\right] \right) \le 0 \: . \end{align*} We conclude that \begin{align*} P[\log f] \le P\left[\log E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}\right] + (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\log E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}\right] \: . \end{align*} Taking the supremum over $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$, we obtain the desired inequality.

A jointly measurable function $f : \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{Y} \to \mathbb{R}_{+, \infty}$ is a conditional e-variable for a set of Markov kernels $H \subseteq (\mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y})$ if $f(x, \cdot)$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{H(x)}$ for all $x \in \mathcal{X}$ (in which $H(x) = \{\eta(x) \mid \eta \in H\}$). We denote the set of conditional e-variables for $H$ by $\mathcal{E}_H$.
nodes.label: def:condEVar

nodes.statement: Let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be a Markov kernel and $H \subseteq (\mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y})$ a set of Markov kernels. A conditional e-variable $f$ for $H$ is a conditional numeraire for $(\kappa, H)$ if for all $x \in \mathcal{X}$, the function $f(x, \cdot)$ is a numeraire for $(\kappa(x), H(x))$. We denote the conditional numeraire for $(\kappa, H)$ by $E^*_{\kappa, H}$ (if it exists).
nodes.label: def:condNumeraire

nodes.statement: If there exists a conditional numeraire for $(\kappa, \{\eta\})$, then $1/E^*_{\kappa, \{\eta\}}$ is a Radon-Nikodym derivative for $\eta$ with respect to $\kappa$.
nodes.label: lem:condNumeraire_singleton

nodes.statement: $1/E^*_{\kappa, \{\eta\}}$ is jointly measurable and satisfies for all $x \in \mathcal{X}$, $1/E^*_{\kappa, \{\eta\}}(x, \cdot) =_{a.e.} \frac{d\eta(x)}{d \kappa(x)}$ since that's the numeraire for a singleton. That's the definition of a Radon-Nikodym derivative of kernels.
If a conditional numeraire exists for $(\kappa, H)$, then $E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, \mathcal{Q} \otimes H} =_{a.e.} E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H}$.
nodes.label: thm:numeraire_compProd_of_condNumeraire

nodes.statement: $E^*_{\kappa, H}$ is a numeraire for $(P \otimes \kappa, \{P\} \otimes H)$, so we get the numeraire property as in Theorem~\ref{thm:numeraire_compProd_le}. We now prove that $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H} \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$. Let $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$ and $\eta \in H$. \begin{align*} (Q \otimes \eta)\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H}\right] &= Q\left[x \mapsto E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}(x) \eta(x)\left[E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}\right] \right] \: . \end{align*} For all $x$, $\eta(x)\left[E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}\right] \le 1$, since $E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}$ is an e-variable for $H(x)$. \begin{align*} (Q \otimes \eta)\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H}\right] &\le Q\left[x \mapsto E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}(x)\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}

Let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be a Markov kernel and $H \subseteq (\mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y})$ a set of Markov kernels. If $\mathcal{X}$ is countable with measurable singletons then there exists a conditional numeraire for $(\kappa, H)$.
nodes.label: lem:exists_condNumeraire_of_countable

nodes.statement: For each $x \in \mathcal{X}$, we can apply Theorem~\ref{thm:exists_numeraire} to the Markov kernel $\kappa(x)$ and the set of kernels $H(x)$ to obtain a numeraire $E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}$. If $\mathcal{X}$ is countable, we can simply take the function $E^*_{\kappa, H}(x,y) = E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}(y)$, and the countability ensures the joint measurability.

Let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be a Markov kernel and $H \subseteq (\mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y})$ a set of Markov kernels. If either $\mathcal{X}$ is countable or $\mathcal{Y}$ is countably generated, then there exists a conditional numeraire for $(\kappa, H)$.
nodes.label: thm:exists_condNumeraire

nodes.statement: The case of countable $\mathcal{X}$ is covered by Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_condNumeraire_of_countable}. (TODO: only for measurable singletons though) TODO: $\kappa \ll H$ hyp? Let's now consider the case where $\mathcal{Y}$ is countably generated. Then there exists a sequence of finer and finer partitions of $\mathcal{Y}$ into finitely many measurable sets $(A_{n,m})_{n \in \mathbb{N}, m \le 2^n}$ with $\mathcal{Y} = \bigcup_{m \le 2^n} A_{n,m}$ for all $n$, and such that the sigma-algebra on $\mathcal{Y}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the sets $A_{n,m}$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the filtration generated by the successive partitions, that is, $\mathcal{F}_n = \sigma(\{A_{n,m} \mid m \le 2^n\})$. TODO

Let $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. The reverse information projection (RIPr) of $P$ onto $\mathcal{Q}$ is the finite measure $P^*_{\mathcal{Q}}$ absolutely continuous with respect to $P$ such that \begin{align*} \frac{dP^*_{\mathcal{Q}}}{dP} = \frac{1}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}} \: . \end{align*} It satisfies $P^*_{\mathcal{Q}}[\mathcal{X}] \le 1$ and the inequality can be strict.
nodes.label: def:ripr

nodes.statement: For a set of probability measures $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$, the effective set of measures $\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the set $\{\mu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{X}) \mid \forall f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}, \: \mu[f] \le 1\}$.
nodes.label: def:effectiveSet

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a set of probability measures. The effective set $\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is convex and satisfies $0 \in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
nodes.label: lem:convex_effectiveSet

nodes.statement: Let $Q \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be a probability measure. Then $\{Q\}_{\mathrm{eff}} = \{Q' \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X}) \mid Q' \le Q\}$, in which $Q' \le Q$ means that $Q'(A) \le Q(A)$ for all measurable sets $A \subseteq \mathcal{X}$.
nodes.label: lem:effectiveSet_singleton

nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \{Q\}_{\mathrm{eff}} &= \{Q' \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X}) \mid \forall f, \ (\forall Q'' \in \{Q\}, Q''[f] \le 1) \implies Q'[f] \le 1\} \\ &= \{Q' \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X}) \mid \forall f, \ Q[f] \le 1 \implies Q'[f] \le 1\} \end{align*} This is the set of finite measures $\{Q' \mid Q' \le Q\}$. Indeed, if $Q' \le Q$, then for all $f$ with $Q[f] \le 1$, $Q'[f] \le Q[f] \le 1$. Conversely, if $Q'$ is such that $(\forall f, \ Q[f] \le 1 \implies Q'[f] \le 1)$, then for any measurable set $A$, we can take the measurable function $f = Q(A)^{-1} \cdot \mathbb{I}_A$ (in which $0^{-1} = \infty$) to obtain $Q'(A) \le Q(A)$.

Let $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be a Markov kernel. Then $\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}} \subseteq (\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q})_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
nodes.label: lem:effectiveSet_comp_subset

nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}} &= \{\kappa \circ Q \mid \forall f, (\forall Q' \in \mathcal{Q}, Q'[f] \le 1) \implies Q[f] \le 1\} \\ (\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q})_{\mathrm{eff}} &= \{R \mid \forall f, (\forall Q' \in \mathcal{Q}, (\kappa \circ Q')[f] \le 1) \implies R[f] \le 1\} \end{align*} Let $\kappa \circ Q \in \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ and $f$ such that $\forall Q' \in \mathcal{Q}, (\kappa \circ Q')[f] \le 1$. That is, $\forall Q' \in \mathcal{Q}, Q'[x \mapsto \kappa(x)[f]] \le 1$. Then since $Q \in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}}$, we have $Q[x \mapsto \kappa(x)[f]] \le 1$. We have proved that $\kappa \circ Q \in (\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q})_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
Let $\mathcal{Q}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{Q}_2 \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two sets of probability measures. Then $\mathcal{Q}_{1, \mathrm{eff}} \subseteq \mathcal{Q}_{2, \mathrm{eff}}$.
nodes.label: lem:effectiveSet_mono

nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{Q}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{Q}_2$ we have $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_2} \subseteq \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:eVarSet_anti}). Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{Q}_{1, \mathrm{eff}} &= \{\mu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{X}) \mid \forall f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1}, \: \mu[f] \le 1\} \\ &\subseteq \{\mu \in \mathcal{M}_+(\mathcal{X}) \mid \forall f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_2}, \: \mu[f] \le 1\} \\ &= \mathcal{Q}_{2, \mathrm{eff}} \: . \end{align*}

Let $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ and $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. If $P \ll \mathcal{Q}$ then \begin{align*} P[\log E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}] = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[\log f] = \inf_{\mu \in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{eff}}} \mathrm{KL}(P, \mu) = \mathrm{KL}(P, P^*_{\mathcal{Q}}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: thm:eVar_KL_duality

nodes.statement: Let $P, Q \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two probability measures with $P \ll Q$. Then \begin{align*} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\{Q\}}} P[\log f] = \mathrm{KL}(P, Q) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:sup_eVar_singleton

nodes.statement: Since $\mathrm{KL}$ is non-increasing in the second argument, \begin{align*} \inf_{Q' \le Q} \mathrm{KL}(P, Q') = \mathrm{KL}(P, Q) \: . \end{align*} Since $\{Q\}_{\mathrm{eff}} = \{Q' \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X}) \mid Q' \le Q\}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:effectiveSet_singleton}), we obtained $\mathrm{KL}(P, Q) = \inf_{Q' \in \{Q\}_{\mathrm{eff}}} \mathrm{KL}(P, Q')$. By the duality of numeraire and $\mathrm{KL}$ divergence (Theorem~\ref{thm:eVar_KL_duality}), we have \begin{align*} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\{Q\}}} P[\log f] = \inf_{Q' \in \{Q\}_{\mathrm{eff}}} \mathrm{KL}(P, Q') = \mathrm{KL}(P, Q) \: . \end{align*}

Let $P, Q \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then for all Markov kernels $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$, \begin{align*} \mathrm{KL}(P, Q) &\ge \mathrm{KL}(\kappa \circ P, \kappa \circ Q) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: thm:dataprocessing_kl

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:sup_eVar_singleton}, $\mathrm{KL}(P, Q) = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\{Q\}}} P[\log f]$. Then by Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_comp_le}, we have \begin{align*} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\{Q\}}} P[\log f] &\ge \sup_{g \in \mathcal{E}_{\{\kappa \circ Q\}}} (\kappa \circ P)[\log g] \: . \end{align*} And that last term is $\mathrm{KL}(\kappa \circ P, \kappa \circ Q)$, again by Lemma~\ref{lem:sup_eVar_singleton}.

The e-Rényi divergence of order $\alpha \in (0,1)$ between two sets of probability measures $\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ is defined as \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}(R, \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \: , \end{align*} for $\mathcal{U}_{\log}$ the max-utility corresponding to the logarithmic utility.
nodes.label: def:erenyiDiv

nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &= \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} \max\left\{\mathcal{U}(R, \mathcal{P}), \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \right\} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:echernoffDiv

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}' \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}' \subseteq \mathcal{Q}$. Then, for all $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}', \mathcal{Q}') &\ge \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_anti

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}' \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}' \subseteq \mathcal{Q}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}', \mathcal{Q}') &\ge \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:echernoffDiv_anti

nodes.statement: Let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be Markov kernel. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\kappa \circ \mathcal{P}, \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}) &\le \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_comp_le

nodes.statement: Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a measurable map. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(f_*\mathcal{P}, f_*\mathcal{Q}) &\le \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_map_le

nodes.statement: Let $\kappa : \mathcal{X} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal{Y}$ be Markov kernel. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\kappa \circ \mathcal{P}, \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}) &\le \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:echernoffDiv_comp_le

nodes.statement: Let $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a measurable map. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(f_*\mathcal{P}, f_*\mathcal{Q}) &\le \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:echernoffDiv_map_le

nodes.statement: For $\alpha \in (0,1)$, if $\mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) < \infty$, then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X}), \: R \ll \mathcal{P}, \: R \ll \mathcal{Q}} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \: . \end{align*} That is, the infimum defining $\mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$ can be restricted to measures $R$ that are absolutely continuous with respect to both $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$. TODO: can we drop the finiteness assumption?
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_eq_iInf_acSet

nodes.statement: If $R$ is not absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathcal{P}$, then $\mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) = \infty$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_eq_top_of_not_acSet}. Similarly, if $R$ is not absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathcal{Q}$, then $\mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) = \infty$. Hence, in both cases, the term $\alpha \mathcal{U_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q})}$ is infinite and does not contribute to the infimum defining $\mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$.

For $\alpha \in (0,1)$, if $\mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) < \infty$ and there exists a measurable set $A$ with $P(A^c) = 0$ and $Q(A^c) = 0$ for all $P \in \mathcal{P}$ and $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X}), \: R(A^c) = 0} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \: . \end{align*} That is, the infimum defining $\mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$ can be restricted to measures $R$ supported on $A$.
nodes.label: cor:erenyiDiv_eq_iInf_support

nodes.statement: We apply Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_eq_iInf_acSet} and note that any measure $R$ that is absolutely continuous with respect to both $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ must satisfy $R(A^c) = 0$.

Let $\phi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ be a measurable embedding. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q}) &= \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_map_eq

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_map_le}, we have $\mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q}) \le \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$. Then either both sides are infinite and we are done, or the left hand side is finite. Let $A = \phi(\mathcal{X}) \subseteq \mathcal{Y}$. Then for all $P \in \mathcal{P}$ and $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, we have $\phi_* P(A^c) = 0$ and $\phi_* Q(A^c) = 0$. By Corollary~\ref{cor:erenyiDiv_eq_iInf_support}, we can restrict the infimum defining $\mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q})$ to measures supported on $A$. Since $\phi$ is an embedding, every measure supported on $A$ is of the form $\phi_* R$ for some $R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ (take $R = \phi^{-1}_* R'$, in which $\phi^{-1}$ is a partial inverse on the range of $\phi$). \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q}) &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R' \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}), \: R'(A^c) = 0} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R', \phi_* \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R', \phi_* \mathcal{Q}) \right) \\ &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \phi_* \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \phi_* \mathcal{Q}) \right) \: . \end{align*} Using then Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_map_eq}, we get \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q}) &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \\ &= \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
\begin{align*} \mathcal{U}(P_1 \otimes P_2, \mathcal{Q}_1 \otimes \mathcal{Q}_2) &= \mathcal{U}(P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1) + \mathcal{U}(P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_prod

nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}_1 \otimes \mathcal{P}_2, \mathcal{Q}_1 \otimes \mathcal{Q}_2) &= \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}_1, \mathcal{Q}_1) + \mathrm{eR}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}_2, \mathcal{Q}_2) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_prod

nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}_1 \otimes \mathcal{P}_2, \mathcal{Q}_1 \otimes \mathcal{Q}_2) &\le \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}_1, \mathcal{Q}_1) + \mathrm{eC}_\alpha(\mathcal{P}_2, \mathcal{Q}_2) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:echernoffDiv_prod_le

nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two sets of probability measures. Suppose that there exists a measurable map $\phi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$ such that $\phi \circ \phi = \mathrm{id}$ and $\phi_* \mathcal{P} = \mathcal{Q}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &= 2 \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X}), \: \phi_* R = R} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_map_swap

nodes.statement: First consider an arbitrary $R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then $R' = \frac{1}{2}(R + \phi_* R)$ satisfies $\phi_* R' = R'$ and by convexity (Lemma~\ref{lem:convex_maxUtility}) and Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_map_swap}, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R', \mathcal{P}) + \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R', \mathcal{Q}) &\le \frac{1}{2} \left( \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \\ &\quad + \frac{1}{2} \left( \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{P}) + \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \\ &= \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*} Hence we can restrict the infimum defining $\mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$ to measures $R$ such that $\phi_* R = R$. For such measures, by Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_map_swap}, $\mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) = \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{P}) = \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P})$ and we get the result.

Let $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two sets of probability measures. Suppose that there exists a measurable map $\phi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$ such that $\phi \circ \phi = \mathrm{id}$ and $\phi_* \mathcal{P} = \mathcal{Q}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &= \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X}), \: \phi_* R = R} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:echernoffDiv_map_swap

nodes.statement: Similar to the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_map_swap}.

Let $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two sets of probability measures. Suppose that there exists a measurable map $\phi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$ such that $\phi \circ \phi = \mathrm{id}$ and $\phi_* \mathcal{P} = \mathcal{Q}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &= 2 \mathrm{eC}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_eq_two_mul_echernoffDiv

nodes.statement: Use Lemmas~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_map_swap} and \ref{lem:echernoffDiv_map_swap}.

Let $a \le b \in [0,1]$. Let $\mathcal{D}_{\le a} = \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \le a\}$ and $\mathcal{D}_{\ge b} = \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \ge b\}$ be sets of distributions on $[0,1]$ with mean constraints. Let $B_{\le a} = \{\mathrm{Ber}(p) \mid p \le a\}$ and $B_{\ge a} = \{\mathrm{Ber}(p) \mid p \ge a\}$ be sets of Bernoulli distributions with the same constraints. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le a}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge b}) &= \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(B_{\le a}, B_{\ge b}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_bounded_eq_erenyiDiv_bernoulli

nodes.statement: First, by Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_anti}, since $B_{\le a} \subseteq \mathcal{D}_{\le a}$ and $B_{\ge b} \subseteq \mathcal{D}_{\ge b}$, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le a}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge b}) &\le \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(B_{\le a}, B_{\ge b}) \: . \end{align*} For the reverse inequality, we use the data processing inequality for e-Rényi divergence (Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_comp_le}). Let $\kappa : [0,1] \rightsquigarrow \{0,1\}$ be the Markov kernel defined by $\kappa(x) = \mathrm{Ber}(x)$ (the Bernoulli distribution with parameter $x$). Then for $P \in \mathcal{P}([0, 1])$, $\kappa \circ P$ is a Bernoulli distribution with parameter $P[\mathrm{id}]$, and thus $\kappa \circ \mathcal{D}_{\le a} = B_{\le a}$ and $\kappa \circ \mathcal{D}_{\ge b} = B_{\ge b}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_comp_le}, \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(B_{\le a}, B_{\ge b}) &\le \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le a}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge b}) \: . \end{align*}

Let $\delta \in [0,1/2]$ and let $B_{\le \delta} = \{\mathrm{Ber}(p) \mid p \le \delta\}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}_{B_{\le \delta}} &= \left\{f : \{0,1\} \to \mathbb{R}_{+, \infty} \text{ measurable} \mid \exists \lambda \in \left[0, \frac{1}{\delta}\right], \: \forall x \in \{0, 1\}, \: f(x) \le 1 + \lambda (x - \delta)\right\} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:eVarSet_bernoulli_le

nodes.statement: It is easy to check that the set on the right is included in $\mathcal{E}_{B_{\le \delta}}$. The constraint on an e-variable $f$ for $B_{\le \delta}$ is that for all $p \le \delta$, \begin{align*} (1 - p) f(0) + p f(1) &\le 1 \: . \end{align*} For $p=0$ and $p=\delta$ we thus get the two constraints \begin{align*} f(0) &\le 1 \: , \\ f(1) &\le 1 + \frac{1 - f(0)}{\delta}(1 - \delta) \: . \end{align*} Let $\lambda = \frac{1 - f(0)}{\delta}$. Then $\lambda \in [0, \frac{1}{\delta}]$ and the second constraint can be rewritten as $f(1) \le 1 + \lambda (1 - \delta)$. We need to check that we also have $f(0) \le 1 + \lambda (0 - \delta)$, but the expression on the right is equal to $f(0)$ by definition of $\lambda$.

Let $\delta \in [0,1/2]$ and let $B_{\le \delta} = \{\mathrm{Ber}(p) \mid p \le \delta\}$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\mathrm{Ber}(1/2), B_{\le \delta}) &= \frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1}{4 \delta (1 - \delta)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:maxUtility_bernoulli_half_le

nodes.statement: We first compute $\mathcal{E}_{B_{\le \delta}}$ with Lemma~\ref{lem:eVarSet_bernoulli_le}. We thus know that we can restrict the supremum over $f \in \mathcal{E}_{B_{\le \delta}}$ to functions of the form $f(x) = 1 + \lambda (x - \delta)$ for some $\lambda \in [0, \frac{1}{\delta}]$. \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\mathrm{Ber}(1/2), B_{\le \delta}) &= \sup_{\lambda \in [0, \frac{1}{\delta}]} \frac{1}{2} \log (1 + \lambda (0 - \delta)) + \frac{1}{2} \log (1 + \lambda (1 - \delta)) \\ &= \frac{1}{2} \log \sup_{\lambda \in [0, \frac{1}{\delta}]} \left((1 - \lambda \delta)(1 + \lambda (1 - \delta))\right) \: . \end{align*} The function $(1 - \lambda \delta)(1 + \lambda (1 - \delta))$ reaches its maximum at $\lambda^* = \frac{1 - 2\delta}{2\delta (1 - \delta)}$ which is in the interval $[0, \frac{1}{\delta}]$ since $\delta \in [0,1/2]$. Its value at the optimum is $\frac{1}{4 \delta (1 - \delta)}$.

Let $\delta \in [0,1/2]$. Let $B_{\le \delta} = \{\mathrm{Ber}(p) \mid p \le \delta\}$ and $B_{\ge 1 - \delta} = \{\mathrm{Ber}(p) \mid p \ge 1 - \delta\}$ be sets of Bernoulli distributions with mean constraints. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(B_{\le \delta}, B_{\ge 1 - \delta}) &= \log \frac{1}{4 \delta (1 - \delta)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_bernoulli

nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:erenyiDiv_map_swap} for the map $\phi : \{0,1\} \to \{0,1\}$ defined by $\phi(0) = 1$ and $\phi(1) = 0$, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(B_{\le \delta}, B_{\ge 1 - \delta}) &= 2 \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\{0,1\}), \: \phi_* R = R} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, B_{\le \delta}) \\ &= 2 \mathcal{U}_{\log}\left(\mathrm{Ber}(1/2), B_{\le \delta}\right) \: . \end{align*} We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_bernoulli_half_le} to conclude.

Let $\delta \in [0,1/2]$. Let $B_{\le \delta} = \{\mathrm{Ber}(p) \mid p \le \delta\}$ and $B_{\ge 1 - \delta} = \{\mathrm{Ber}(p) \mid p \ge 1 - \delta\}$ be sets of Bernoulli distributions with mean constraints. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}(B_{\le \delta}, B_{\ge 1 - \delta}) &= \frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1}{4 \delta (1 - \delta)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:echernoffDiv_bernoulli

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_eq_two_mul_echernoffDiv}, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}(B_{\le \delta}, B_{\ge 1 - \delta}) &= \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(B_{\le \delta}, B_{\ge 1 - \delta}) \: . \end{align*} We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_bernoulli} to conclude.

Let $\delta \in [0,1/2]$. Let $\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta} = \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \le \delta\}$ and $\mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta} = \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \ge 1 - \delta\}$ be sets of distributions on $[0,1]$ with mean constraints. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) &= \log \frac{1}{4 \delta (1 - \delta)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:erenyiDiv_bounded

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_bounded_eq_erenyiDiv_bernoulli}, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) &= \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(B_{\le \delta}, B_{\ge 1 - \delta}) \: . \end{align*} We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_bernoulli} to conclude.

Let $\delta \in [0,1/2]$. Let $\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta} = \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \le \delta\}$ and $\mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta} = \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \ge 1 - \delta\}$ be sets of distributions on $[0,1]$ with mean constraints. Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) &= \frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1}{4 \delta (1 - \delta)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:echernoffDiv_bounded

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_eq_two_mul_echernoffDiv}, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) &= \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) \: . \end{align*} We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_bounded} to conclude.

Let $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two sets of probability measures. Suppose that there exists a measurable function $f_0 : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ which is less than 1 and $\delta \in [0,1/2]$ such that \begin{align*} \forall P \in \mathcal{P}, \: P[f_0] &\le \delta \: , \\ \forall Q \in \mathcal{Q}, \: Q[f_0] &\ge 1 - \delta \: . \end{align*} Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \log \frac{1}{4\delta(1 - \delta)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: thm:erenyiDiv_lower_bound

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_map_le} for the function $f_0$, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*} $f_0 \circ \mathcal{P} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \le \delta\}$ and $f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \ge 1 - \delta\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_anti}, we thus have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \mathrm{eR}_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) \: . \end{align*} We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_bounded} to conclude.

Let $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two sets of probability measures. Suppose that there exists a measurable function $f_0 : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ which is less than 1 and $\delta \in [0,1/2]$ such that \begin{align*} \forall P \in \mathcal{P}, \: P[f_0] &\le \delta \: , \\ \forall Q \in \mathcal{Q}, \: Q[f_0] &\ge 1 - \delta \: . \end{align*} Then \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1}{4\delta(1 - \delta)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: thm:echernoffDiv_lower_bound

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_map_le} for the function $f_0$, we have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \mathrm{eC}(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*} $f_0 \circ \mathcal{P} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \le \delta\}$ and $f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\mathrm{id}] \ge 1 - \delta\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_anti}, we thus have \begin{align*} \mathrm{eC}(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \mathrm{eC}(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) \: . \end{align*} We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_bounded} to conclude.
